articles.title: 'Era Of One-Sided Deals Over': Iran Pounds U.S. Bases, Then Signals Collapse Of Negotiations

articles.title: ON CAM: Exact Moment Ro Khanna Was Detained By Armed Israeli Settlers; ‘Scared For My Life...’
articles.description: Congressman Ro Khanna has claimed he was briefly detained by armed Israeli settlers while visiting the occupied West Bank, describing the incident as a stark example of the realities Palestinians face under Israeli occupation. Khanna said settlers armed with US-made rifles blocked his delegation's vehicle before Israeli soldiers arrived, alleging the military sided with the settlers rather than the American delegation. The California Democrat said the experience exposed what he called a culture of "impunity" and raised fresh questions about US military aid and Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank. Israeli authorities have not publicly responded to Khanna's account.

articles.description: FBI Director Kash Patel is at the center of fresh political controversy after reports claimed he abruptly canceled a planned trip to Chicago following a last-minute summons to the White House. The visit, reportedly tied to an FBI field office stop and a country music concert featuring his girlfriend Alexis Wilkins, was allegedly scrapped while Patel's plane was already on the tarmac. Reports suggest some Trump administration officials had grown concerned over Patel's recent travel and public actions, though both the FBI and the White House have strongly denied any internal rift. Patel has dismissed the reports as "fake news," saying the public will soon learn why he was at the White House. The controversy comes as congressional Democrats continue scrutinizing Patel over allegations of misuse of government resources, claims the FBI says are completely false.

articles.title: Pentagon’s Biggest Battle: Not Iran, But Beards? Hegseth’s Shock Obsession Rocks US Military
articles.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has intensified his crackdown on beards in the U.S. military, ordering stricter enforcement of grooming standards and tighter scrutiny of medical and religious exemptions. The move follows reports that Hegseth was dissatisfied after seeing multiple bearded sailors during a visit to a Navy ship. The Trump administration argues the policy is about discipline, professionalism and military readiness, while critics say the changes could disproportionately affect service members who require beard exemptions for medical conditions such as pseudofolliculitis barbae or for religious reasons. The renewed push has reignited debate over appearance standards across America's armed forces.
